# `cycle-count` commands

## `cycle-count classify`

Propose cycle classes from cost of goods issued over a period (default the last 12 months to today), the ABC way: ranked by issued cost, the items making the first 80% (a_share) are A, the next 15% (b_share) B, the rest C, an item that issued nothing C. Count differences and inventory adjustments do not count as issued. The dry run lists each item, its share and its proposed class; running it sets the classes as item updates. Example: `bookflow cycle-count classify --dry-run`.

A dry run previews the proposed result without saving it. Any proposed record IDs or posted status in that preview describe the prospective save, not an existing saved record.

| Scope | company |

| Required role | standard |
| Capability | item |
| Feature | — |
| HTTP | `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/cycle-count.classify` |
| External binary body | none |

### CLI

`bookflow cycle-count classify --date-to 2026-12-31 --dry-run --company "Demo Plumbing Co" --json`

## `cycle-count due`

What should we count this week? The items due for a cycle count at a site: an item is due when its class interval has passed since its last recorded count there, or it has never been counted there (unclassified items never are) -- then it has been due since it was first stocked there. Ranked by days overdue over the class interval, so a late A item comes before an equally late C item. A count of bins counts an item only when every bin holding it was counted. Count the first ones with `inventory-count create --site <site> --cycle --limit 25`; places left over take items falling due within the next six days. Example: `bookflow cycle-count due --site Warehouse`.
